frontier.hypothesis: A REGISTER-valued ninth reference for `i` closes the i-FIRST order outright: nine flow-counted references put i at 27/95 = 2842, clear of tbl's 2553 ceiling, in the definition order that already produces target's preamble emission - and it needs no change to tbl, out2, stptr, stptr2, saved, pa4 or a3.
frontier.mechanism: E-s9-9's refined survival rule - a self-update `i = i OP x` with a REGISTER-valued operand and at least one intervening statement survives cse1 into flow (constants are folded, fresh intermediates are copy-propagated), is counted at flow.c:2081, and is merged back by combine before any byte is emitted. Placed inside i's dead hole in the between-loops block it also costs zero live length.
frontier.next_probe: Find a register-valued spelling of loop2's starting index. Note loop1 exits with i already equal to 0x12, so `i = 0x12;` is arithmetically a no-op there - look for a derivation from a value live at that point (a1/a2 after their 0x6C advance, stptr, saved) rather than from a literal, and read `Register 78 used N times across M insns` in .lreg. Also try the self-update inside loop1 (an `i++` split with a register operand), which adds +1 to tbl's live length as well and would land the 2500/2500 tie from the other side. tmp/grind/func_80041188/s9/run.sh turns each variant into one ~1s cc1 run and prints both the priority table and the seat verdict.

frontier.hypothesis: A surviving block-0 insn whose donor already holds a callee-saved seat gives the i-FIRST order its single missing insn, without creating a tenth register claimant.
frontier.mechanism: Same cse1 self-update rule; the requirement from E-s9-7/8 is exactly one insn that survives cse1 into flow and sits after tbl's definition in block 0, and the constraint is that the donor's priority must stay in its target rank band so the seat order is untouched. `saved` is the wrong donor because target spills it; `stptr` (7/41 = 3414, comfortably top of the table) and `pa4` (7/95, seated in $s7) are the right shape of donor.
frontier.next_probe: Enumerate self-update spellings of `stptr` and `pa4` in block 0 and read tbl's live length for each. stptr's separated split has been measured in three placements and gives +1 ref / +3 live with no added insn - vary the number and identity of the intervening statements, since the survival rule is sensitive to exactly that. Accept a donor whose priority rises but keeps its rank position; reject any that adds a new register claimant (watch for `saved` leaving the spilled state in the seat checker).

frontier.hypothesis: Spelling pa4/out2/out3 through a real PsyQ `MATRIX *` local is byte-neutral and materially reduces the layer-1 exposure of every form built on the I2 chassis (carried over from s8, still unspent).
frontier.mechanism: a4 addresses two adjacent 0x20-byte objects and PsyQ's MATRIX is 0x20 bytes; func_8004A348(buf, m) builds a rotation matrix and func_800523E0(m0, m1, a3, dst) consumes the pair, so the natural original source is `MATRIX *m = (MATRIX *)a4;` with `&m[0]` / `&m[1]`, and a second loop that re-takes `&m[1]` before it starts reads as ordinary scoping rather than as a dead-store re-init.
frontier.next_probe: Re-spell candidate.c and the M1 variant (rejected/m1-i2-symk-ilate-alltarget-seats-preamble-order4.c) with a MATRIX-typed - or equivalent 0x20-byte struct - local and confirm the .lreg table and the seat verdict are unchanged. If they are, adopt that spelling everywhere BEFORE stacking any further construct, because the frontier-1 and frontier-2 forms will otherwise combine a re-init, a sym-K chain and block-0 staging in one diff.
